summary: fractal doctor runs its store checks together, so on a busy store a slow check costs its own 15 s and no check goes unrun; the claim-signatures count finds held claims through a new index instead of reading every count row

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay change.

schema.detail: Additive and local: the index claim_signature_counts_held_index on claim_signature_counts(candidates, claim_id) WHERE candidates>32. It is outside the claim log, shared projections and digests. The schema version is unchanged. If an older build opens the store after a rollback, it keeps the index and never reads it. SQLite maintains it as claims gain candidates, and that is harmless.

compatibility.detail: GET /v1/doctor returns the same checks in the same order with the same statuses. More checks finish on a busy store, so fewer report timeout.

downtime.detail: Once, at the first start after upgrading, the store builds the new index before the daemon serves, and logs how long it took ("built the index of claims with many signature candidates in N s"). On a 56 GB store with 2.9 million signed claims, it took 9.5 s cold and 0.3 s warm. Later starts find the index and skip it.

recovery.detail: Rolling back is safe: the previous release runs doctor's checks one after another and leaves the index in place, as described under schema.
